Greenlight Planet Sun King Pro an Portable Solar Lantern Plus USB Charger This is my 3rd Sun King Solar Light, but my 1st Sun King Pro2 model and I'm happy to report that the SK2 model does everything the original did but also includes the very useful ability to charge cell phones or mobile devices such as tablets or laptops as well (and fairly quickly too).

The Sun King Solar Lights are used extensively in remote areas of Africa or India where residents lack access to electricity, but their usefulness is not limited to those purposes at all because they are extremely handy to have on hand here in America as well for applications like camping trips, night lights, to save money by using them instead of electric lights, or for emergency lighting in case the power is out!

Offering 3 settings, the lowest setting is bright enough to act to light hallways well enough to act as a nightlight & provide safe navigation of rooms in case of power outage (and can last for 36 hrs on a full charge). The other settings are brighter and you can position the lamp on its stand to act as a reading light or point it upwards instead towards the ceiling to light up an entire room. In fact, the light is so versatile that you could also remove it from the stand and hang it from a wall or ceiling hook inside the house or in a tent if so desired and it provides good lighting all night when charged.

The solar panel is small enough to be conveniently moved around effortlessly, comes with a long enough power cord to reach the lamp for charging, has an easy to read display that lets you know if you're getting enough sun strength in the current position or whether you need to adjust the angle more and also lets you know whether the light is fully charged or not.

15 times brighter than a typical kerosene lamp (and totally safe to use), with convenient dual USB ports, Sun King Pro 2 can charge a phone while simultaneously powering an additional appliance or a second phone plus it has a five-year battery lifetime. It's light enough to charge & position effortlessly and yet extremely well made and durable.

I not only recommend the Sun King Pro2 Solar Lights to my friends - I intend to buy more for my home as well!
text_fidelity_b: Greenlight Planet Sun King Pro an Portable Solar Lantern Plus USB Charger

text_fidelity_a:
Body Bar Power & Grace DVD This workout uses both a body bar and the gliding disks. Instructor Mindy Mylrea is joined by Keli Roberts, who modifies some of the exercises, and Violet Zaki, who increases the intensity.

Mylrea starts with a long (about 7 minutes) warm-up. During the warm-up, you are just holding the body bar and not really using it for resistance. In addition, she does not step on the disks until about halfway through the warm-up; at that time, she incorporates added moves such as twists plus side and back lunges.

For the standing portion of the workout, Mylrea takes greater advantage of the body bar. The option is often to hold the bar at the chest, on the shoulders, or overhead while performing classic strength moves such as side and front lunges, curtsey lunges, and deadlifts. The standing segment ends with push-up/plank work with the feet on the disks.

The floor work is shorter (18 minutes), but it continues to focus on the lower body with bridges and other moves targeting the hamstrings. Mylrea also includes abs work and a nice floor stretch (6 minutes), bringing in the entire workout right around 54 minutes.

I really enjoy Mylrea's original Gliding set, as I like mixing and matching from the 3 workouts on that DVD. For some reason, this workout didn't click as well with me, even though there aren't any major problems with the workout itself. One issue is that I do not have a body bar; substituting an unweighted stick and dumbbells worked okay, but this took some fun out of the workout. I also think that I have moved away from these type of cardio/strength circuit workouts now that I have discovered kettlebells.

For those who own both a body bar and gliding disks, however, I would recommend this DVD.
text_fidelity_b: Body Bar Power & Grace DVD

Wahoo RFLKT+ Bike Computer for iPhone & Android This RFLKT+ bike computer worked great with my iPhone 5, especially once I figured out how to use it! the instructions are bad - as in they have a small piece of paper in the box that tells you to scan the code to get to the instructions. I understand the reasoning - "technology changes fast and we want you to have the most up to date instructions." Okay, but sadly the instructions did not match the version of the device that I had, so I had to figure out some of it on my own. I mean you'd think they would keep the online instructions up to date if that's the reason they want you to go online to get them. I would have appreciated a brief "quick start" paper instruction inside the box.

Okay, enough about the instructions. Once I figured it out, this little device collected flawless from my iphone although you need to keep the app active or else the device shuts down. think of it as an extension of your iphone screen - a second monitor. I also have a Garmin heart rate monitor (ANT+) and a Garmin speed/cadence sensor (ANT+) on my bike. the Wahoo found both of those quickly and displayed the data accurately. I matched it against my Garmin 310XT watch and it matched up perfectly.

The one thing I had to remember was to start the app on the phone in order to get the distance and time to start recording! I was cruising along and watching my heart rate and cadence but couldn't figure out why the mileage wasn't getting logged until I realized I hadn't started things up on the iPhone. So this works well, and if you've already got other apps and like using your iphone then this is a great little device.
text_fidelity_b: Wahoo RFLKT+ Bike Computer for iPhone & Android

text_fidelity_a:
KUGOO Electric Scooter, 800W Motor Off-Road Scooter, 10-INCH Pneumatic Tires Up to 25 MPH Motorized Adult Scooter, Electric Scooter for Adults, Pro Scooter, G2 PRO I have 7 scooters I've collected along the way to review and hands down this is the most fun one out there! If you're familiar with how an electric scooter works then this one is just like the others and will be easy to setup and get going. Took me about five minutes to unbox and get going! Even for newbies this scooter is plenty easy to setup!

One of the favorite things I love on this are the giant wheels- we ride on a concrete trail several miles across town and this absolutely grabs onto the concrete very well and is a better overall ride! My one complaint is the tires must be thin as on my fourth ride, one of them got a flat even though I didn't hit anything noticeable like glass or a screw. Nothing in the tire but it just started losing pressure on a ride and within a couple minutes the tire was completely flat and I was stuck pushing it home a mile. My suggestion is to get the tire size off the tire and immediately swap them out for solid tires! The air tires are a slightly smoother ride but you'll regret it when you're stuck pushing it home...
Edit: The air leaks out of the valve stem. I went to add some green slime and it did hold air but when I moved the valve stem, air comes out at the bottom of it... So the valve stem was faulty and the slime didn't help anything. I've been searching like crazy with no luck finding a solid tire to replace these with. Should have been on the scooter to begin with in my opinion.

Speed wise, I got this monster up to 29 mph and I'm a larger man (260 pounds) so that's a testament to this thing! It stands higher than your average scooter too which is weird at first but I fell in love with the added height nearly instantly!

It has a faster startup than other scooters that require more of a kick start. Which- be careful, that can be dangerous if you have the scooter on and are pushing it to park it before turning it off. I almost flipped mine backwards onto myself this way, it happens QUICK. So definitely turn the scooter (and any scooter) off before pushing around.

Battery life is fantastic- we ride several miles across town and back and I still have half a battery left after that!

Overall this is my favorite thing I've gotten on review and I've gotten big fancy electronics like big TVs, computers, etc... But this is my favorite toy I've grabbed, I HIGHLY recommend it! In the future I'll absolutely be buying another from this company!
text_fidelity_b: KUGOO Electric Scooter, 800W Motor Off-Road Scooter, 10-INCH Pneumatic Tires Up to 25 MPH Motorized Adult Scooter, Electric Scooter for Adults, Pro Scooter, G2 PRO

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Surge Fitness Superwatch, Black, Small (US Version) I have had my Surge since mid-Dec and I am happy to say it is a huge step up from the Flex! I am so excited that I don't have a collection of stuff on my wrist anymore (and that is what it felt like to have a watch and another device on my wrist).

So far, things have been overall great!

The Size
It is a bit more bulky than my beloved watch, so it does catch on long sleeves. It is a little annoying to try and view it when I am wearing a jacket, but it is a small annoyance that I can live with. I don't find it bothersome to wear while I am sitting at my computer (which I did have a problem with when I wore my watch). I bought a size small, which fits well, but I probably could have gotten away with a large (despite the fact that I have tiny wrists and it is a fraction of an inch smaller than the recommended size for large).

Style
It is by no-means femenine, but as far as fitness watches go, it is generally unisex. I also don't have the gap that I usually have with fitness devices where my wrist curves but my watch face doesn't, so I end up with gaps under the top and bottom of the face, so that is a definite plus (there is a small gap, but not annoyingly bad).

Function
As a watch, it is one of the best executions of a watch on a fitness device that I have seen. I would love to see the screen have the option to default back to the time screen. It currently stays on whichever screen you last viewed, so sometimes that is frustrating, but nothing insurmountable.

The backlight is spot on. The sensitivity seems to be perfect so I have yet to look at my watch and not see what it is trying to tell me.

Notifications are good, but it only does calls and texts. I am not sure I really need more notifications, personally. I get a lot of notifications through the day and would get annoyed if I got notifications for each facebook post or email.

Tracking seems to be fairly accurate. Heart rate has been within reason (ie, not really far from what my heart rate should me). Some people need to move the tracker higher up on their wrists, but I haven't had that issue yet. Of course, you can spoof steps if you are determined or animated, you can certainly spoof steps, but then again, I know that sometimes my steps aren't counted right, so I figure it all evens out at the end of the day.

Food tracking is decent, but there are better food trackers out there. Luckily, fitbit does work with other services to provide 2 way integration of food tracking (and other stats).

The exercise settings do allow a lot of options for how you would like to work out. Biking is not currently available, which doesn't bother me, but there are plenty of people out there who want it back. Of course, there is nothing keeping you from using another workout type to at least consolidate your statistics. The GPS is ok. I have noticed that GPS can be inaccurate when you are around a lot of buildings.

Music control works. Not much to see there.

Apps and web dashboard are great. There is a lot of information that is usually presented in an understandable way. There are a couple logs like heart rate that do not populate with your data, but you can see the information on the dashboard with a decent degree of granularity, so it isn't a huge deal. Presumably, this should be corrected by the time this device is officially released.

The battery is supposed to last up to 7 days. I haven't made it more than 4, but I recently changed settings like bluetooth for music (which I don't use) and made sure to turn off my alarms that I don't use and don't wake up to.

I would urge you not to purchase this until it is released unless you can find it from a retailer (ie Target, Best Buy, or REI) since people are selling them for more than twice their retail cost.

I definitely recommend it! Even at this point, I am very satisified with it!

UPDATE - The Surge is officially available today (1/6) - Check with retailers, but if you can't find it, it is definitely on the Fitbit site!
Also, I added pictured to the review to show the fit. My wrist is about 6.1 inches and this is a size small. The small is supposed to fit 5.5-6.7 inches. The large is supposed to fit 6.3-7.9 inches. I think I would have been able to get away with the large (there is at least an inch of strap holes left on mine), but happy with my decision on the small!
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Surge Fitness Superwatch, Black, Small (US Version)

text_fidelity_a:
Arrow Precision Inferno Wildfire Crossbow Package (225-Pounds) I've been hunting with Mathews compound bows for 20 years and reached a point in my age that I wanted to switch to a crossbow. I wanted to find the best bow for the money to start out. I like compounds but I wanted to stay as basic and simple as I could with the crossbow for service and maintaining accuracy so I wanted a recurve.
Long story short the Excaliburs are nice but to rich for my blood so I took a chance on the Wildfire II based on the reviews. I'm glad that I did.
Pros:
Excellent fit and finsh work on the entire bow. Definitely quality construction on par with any of the big name crossbow makers.
It seems as fast and they say it is. Once sighted in it is consistently accurate. I think this bow is on par with the Excalibur baseline bows Like the Axiom or Ibex if not better as this bow has a one peice Aluminum rail versus a plastic rail. Weight is not bad at all and it feels well balanced for free hand shooting. Soft touch Camo is awesome and a nice balance of pattern and color.
Thumb Safety just like a rifle. Not up on the side of the string latch like a lot of other crossbows and quiet as a mouse. Not a loud CLICK! when you take the safety off. The trigger does have some creep but is pretty smooth overall. The more I shoot the better it gets.
Shot noise is average and less than a pellet gun for comparison. It comes with factory installed limb dampeners that attach to the riser/limb. I also installed the SIMS LIMBSAVER kit and it definitely helped reduce the sound when fired.
Scope is actually very good quality and clarity. Super clean reticle and the adjustable illumination is great for early morning/late evening shots! I was thinking to buy a Nikon but this scope is really nice so I will keep using it.
Rope cocker, Arrows, quiver, and sling are very nice quality as well. Super sling swivels too!
Must haves:
Plano Soft bow case. Best priced case that actually fits the bow another really good option is the OMP Crossbow soft case. A little more in cost but has additional pockets for arrows etc.
Tenpoint ACUrope cocker (BEST). Compact and retractable. Works like a dream and has a belt pouch.
Carbon Express Bolts. Either the Piledrivers or if you want the best get the Maxima Hunters. Buy their lighted nocks for your hunting arrows.
Go ahead and buy the MTM bolt case for your extra bolts.
Scorpion Venom string wax. The bow comes with string wax but I feel the Scorpion is easier to use and stays super slick in all weather.
Rail lube. DO NOT USE STRING WAX! I did and it slowed down the bow and killed my accuracy. I had to clean the rail with rubbing alcohol and start over. Buy Excalibur rail lube and/or do some research on the bow forums on what the veteran shooters are using. Some recommend silicone spray and other types of lube. If you're going to hunt use something that doesn't have any odor. I ended up using Ultralube 4x. It's all natural and no odor.
NAP 100 grain Sptifire Edge mechanical broadheads. These are my personal favorite and for overall accuracy I prefer mechanicals over fixed blades for better flight at high speeds.
Target for field point is the Hurricane H25 hands down best practice target for the money. It stops the bolts no matter what and is heavy and stable. You don't need a stand for it.
Target for broadheads I recommend the Blobtarget or American white tale HybriMAT AP . They are both pricey (BT 18"x18"x10" $90 shppied) (HybriMAT AP 18"x18"x12" $129.95 shipped) but they will last you for years and years vs the cheaper ones that last a year and are still very expensive!
Update:
Bought a Prochrono on Amazon to check the speed of the bow and right now it is 315fps with the stock arrows and with the Maxima Hunters. Dyna Flight string should bring it up to as much as 330fps.
I ended up removing the limbsavers since they slowed it down (10fps!) and actually created vibration in the bow after the shot. To be honest the noise level is not much different without them.
Another update. Bow is shooting 330fps using Carbon Express 20" hunter maximas and 100gr tips. I switched to Black Eagle Spynal Tapp arrows and the speed is still on.
Final deer season tally is 3 does and i buck
text_fidelity_b: Arrow Precision Inferno Wildfire Crossbow Package (225-Pounds)

text_fidelity_a:
Sanlan Resistance Bands Set with Workout Bar, Pilates Bar Kit Exercise Elastic Bands with Handles & Door Anchor for Full Body Strength Training, Home Gym Equipment If you’re someone who wants a strength- based workout, you know that using weights is the normal and common way to go. If you don’t have weights, there is an alternative that some say is just as good, and that is using resistance bands like this set, sold by the Sanlan Store.

With this set, you get multiple bands, a bar to hook them on, and a few accessories like ankle straps, handles, and a door anchor. The bands, colored yellow, green, red, blue, and black, offer different levels of resistance. You can start out low, with just a band or two, then gradually combine more bands for a more strenuous workout.

Using resistance bands is something completely new to me and there are many good reasons to like this or even prefer this to using actual weights. The top reason is the ease of working out anytime, anyplace. Because there is no actual weight, you can take your carrying bag and bands most anywhere. They are lightweight and take up little space. You can then remove them from the bag, hook the bands to the bar, and begin your workout. I don’t really have any basis for comparison, since this is something new to me, but the bands are durable and made to last. I don’t have any worries that they will break, so I can workout with peace of mind.

Some exercise bands are nothing more than bands, but this set comes complete with a bar, so it’s all set for you to use. Of course, you don’t have to use the bar- there are other exercises you can do that do not require the bar. But I like that the set has everything you need for a varied workout.

Free weights, barbells, and dumbbells are still the most common way to weight train, but there is something to be said for using resistance bands instead. I feel safer using these bands than I do using free weights and I like that I can easily take them most anyplace. It’s a quality set and a good one for those who want to improve their physical fitness.
text_fidelity_b: Sanlan Resistance Bands Set with Workout Bar, Pilates Bar Kit Exercise Elastic Bands with Handles & Door Anchor for Full Body Strength Training, Home Gym Equipment

Expands outward so if you pack this full it may end up being unsafe for hiking whereas the center of gravity and position of pack may cause you to fall over backward.

No adjustment for repositioning pack down/up between shoulders and hips.

If you are tall/large (6'1" / 250lbs) this pack cannot be adjusted to ride on hips and small of your back, where 80% of the weight of gear should be positioned. All the weight of the pack hangs on the shoulders.

It may not fit over winter clothing, especially if you are fairly large person.

There is no way to secure to the bottom other gear such a tent, sleeping bag, or even a bedroll, which would help some with weight distribution.

Summary: Great for people with small/medium body frame. Not really suitable for big and tall.
text_fidelity_b: CVLIFE Tactical Backpack Military Army Rucksack 60L Large Assault Pack Detachable Molle Bag…

iBert Child Bicycle Safe-T-Seat My daughter and I love this seat. I bought it because I did not want to haul a heavy trailer.

It is installed on my beach cruiser and it fits perfectly - plenty of room for me to reach the handlebars and pedal without the bike seat in the way. I am 5'4" short. It was easy to install. I am surprised at how stable and natural it feels.

I bought it when she was 10 months old, but she was too small to use it. I started using it when she was just over 1 yr and she fit much better (she is average size).

So far we do short rides around the neighborhood in the evenings and weekends and I can take her 1.5 miles to daycare, and she loves it. She can also look up and see me and ring the bell. We can talk about the things we see on the ride, unlike if we had a trailer.

She has fallen asleep twice while riding. There is nowhere for her head to go, but to slump sideways. I have just supported her head with my hand for the few minutes it takes me to get home.

One very nice aspect to this seat is that it mounts on the bike stem, so when she grabs the handlebars, she can't get any torque to steer the bike.

Mine came with the padding for the seat.

Cons:
The shoulder straps are a little strange - they can slide off her shoulder, but this won't be a problem when she is bigger.

The bar that comes down over the child's lap has a cheap attachment mechanism. This ought to be fixed in the next models - it is not acceptable for a product this expensive.

In a light rain (like we encountered last weekend), water puddles in the bottom of the foot cups - I might drill a hole on the bottom of each one (we live in the Pacific NorthWest).
text_fidelity_b: iBert Child Bicycle Safe-T-Seat

text_fidelity_a:
Pelican Self Inflating Sleeping Pad w/Pillow & Arm Rest, Camping Gear - Waterproof Foldable Lightweight Air Mattress - Memory Foam Sleeping Mat for Hiking, Backpacking - Travel Accessories - Black I use Pelican cases for work all the time, so I was intrigued at how they would handle camping gear like this. At first I was a little bit disappointed in the "self inflation" part. But once I understood what it means, I really do appreciate it now.
The only truly inflatable part are the side bars (which prevent you from rolling off the mat) and the pillow part. The middle is just memory foam with a familiar looking Pelican style valve on the bottom. If you've ever bought a memory foam mattress online, you know how this works- it comes in a vacuum sealed bag devoid of air, but once you cut it the air whooshes in and the mattress inflates to normal size. That's sort of what this "self inflation" is. You open the valve, the memory foam inside puffs itself up and becomes a more comfortable mat that is noticeably thicker than it was a moment ago. Seal the valve back up, and you can lie down on it and it honestly feels better than it looks!
Once you are done using it, allow the air to leave the side pockets and pillow, release the valve at the bottom, and roll it up. While rolling it, the air will leave the valve at the bottom, and when you've reached the end, just close the valve again to seal it from trying to open and inflate again. It's actually a pretty smart design once you understand it, I just didn't know what to expect before it arrived. I hope this review helps explain it to future buyers who might be expecting a larger self inflating mattress.
text_fidelity_b: Pelican Self Inflating Sleeping Pad w/Pillow & Arm Rest, Camping Gear - Waterproof Foldable Lightweight Air Mattress - Memory Foam Sleeping Mat for Hiking, Backpacking - Travel Accessories - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Swiss Cargo SCKJ02Q02 3 in 1 Kayak Carrier, Black I just got these (5/27/18) so I will be coming back to edit after next weekend when I use these for a two hour drive on the freeway, but for now I wanted to leave a review because of the 'screws not lining up' that I'm seeing on so many reviews.

I bought mine at Dunham's, which are already "seconds" so if anything I'd expect things like screws not quite lining up, but I think those reviewers just made the same assumption I did at first: that you install the two screws through the middle holes in the flat rubber bottom. That is incorrect!! The screws actually go in diagonal holes to form half of an X. I found that it really created a nice grip and being on a diagonal meant the maximum surface area possible of the attachy bit hugging my crossbars. So just an FYI - I wouldn't put a lot of stock in the "holes not lining up" reviews. One glance at the directions shows you how to properly attach the screws at opposite corners. Also note that the teeth on the middle bar may not tightly lock together right out of the box. Mine didn't. But then I realized that the red thing that locks them down also rotates to loosen or tighten those teeth together so now everything is good and locked.

EDIT: I'm back to give my review - I actually returned these. Problems I found: 1. the bottom of the J is flat instead of in the actual J shape. Seems like that would make it easier to load but it doesn't because if you put it in the center of your roof to use with two kayaks it is pretty far from the edge of your roof so lifting the kayak into the holder becomes difficult just due to how much roof you have to clear before you reach the rack, and sliding the kayak on from the rear doesn't work either because of the flat instead of actual J design, so there is nothing holding your kayak onto the device when you slide it up onto the roof and it just falls over the side of the car. You need someone else to at least spot the kayak to make sure it doesn't fall so this carrier requires two people.

The second issue is that it is very small. If you have two little 8 footers it should be fine but if you have an Old Towne or a Wilderness or really any brand of fishing kayak you are only going to be able to fit one in this holder because without that J shape you have to lean the center bracket way back to hold your wider kayak without it plunging back to the ground before you can ever get it fastened up.

The one thing I liked was the way it attached to the cross bars. That diagonal design AND the way they designed it so one side has a typical screw hole but the other side is a non-closed hole so you can screw on both bolts and then swing the underneath 'arm' onto the second bolt and tighten to your crossbars, makes it easier than trying to start the screw/bolt from completely unattached while on a roof of a car. It's hard to explain without seeing it, but you'll have to take my word that it's a nice feature the makers obviously considered when designing the product.

It did hold my kayak securely (with the center bar at about 145 degrees), I just didn't see a point in keeping a holder for two kayaks when it would only hold one of my kayak's size. I used these on ROLA aftermarket crossbars, aero shaped 3.5", found here on Amazon and it fit very well on those bars. Construction I would say is excellent.
text_fidelity_b: Swiss Cargo SCKJ02Q02 3 in 1 Kayak Carrier, Black

Kodiak Canvas Flex-Bow Canvas Tent Deluxe LOVE LOVE LOVE this tent!!!
We have previously owned the classic cheaper coleman tents and when ours wore out, we bought a new coleman... upon opening it, it had tears in the seams...I boxed it up and sent it back. We were so upset by the lack of craftsmanship we decided to research better quality canvas tents. We are a young family and liked the idea of a tent that we could use for years to come. We decided on the 10x14, it's very spacious and we are able to set up a queen, and twin air mattress with plenty of room to store our bags/totes and a large dog/bed. I am a petite lady and I was able to put this tent up by myself (only took 25 min from box to erect, while stopping to look at the directions) it is a very heavy tent, but I was able to put it up with a bit of effort.
Once up I was able to really get a look at this tent... WOW! This tent is large and heavy duty! The floor is a thick rubber-like material that you can tell isn't gonna leak (and it didn't, even when there were puddles of rain water between the tarp below and tent) I sprayed the tent down (as per directions) prior to our first camping trip. And off we went...
This tent has turned heads every time we camp, it is a heavy duty, quality tent that we know will last for years to come... It is so simple to put up, and we are so pleased with our investment.
We have not yet had it stand the test of a storm, but I have no doubt it will hold up well.
As far as staying warm, the larger tent makes it difficult to stay warm, so bundle up and use warm blankets ;)

Oh, did I mention the tent storage bag?!?! It's awesome, and your tent will always fit, no need for super tight refilling to make it fit in the bag, this bag adjusts and will always fit your rolled up tent (we fold in half, then half again, roll and adjust the bag to fit )

To summarize:
Pros:
Large roomy tent that you can stand and walk around in, the walls are straight so you don't lose storage room
Durable canvas that is waterproof
Quality thick floor that will not leak
Heavy duty metal rods/poles and steaks
Large doors and windows makes the tent feel even more open and allows a cross breeze
The ingenious tent bag that will always be able to fit the tent once rolled up

Cons:
The long poles (when storing) and the weight of the tent
No electrical slot for extension cords (have to put them through the door)

Overall If you are in the market for a quality tent that will last for years to come...buy this tent!

Sevylor Mesa Stand Up Paddleboard I am new to SUP. This board has been perfect for a beginner. It was easy to set up, easy to store, easy to transport, and easy to SUP. The board came with a pump (to inflate and deflate the board), a bag (to transport and store the empty board), an ankle leash, a repair kit, and a bungee (attached to the top front of the board for storage).

The board deflated is pretty heavy. The bag that comes with the board is backpack style and makes it easy to carry, even with all my other gear and kids.

The pump worked easily and quickly. My pressure valve on my pump did not work, so I just had to guess and hope for the best when inflating.

The 3 fins on the board make it easy to stay on a forward path. They do make it a little more difficult to turn, but made it simple to stand and paddle in a straight direction without much practice.

I also tried out a hard "beginners" board from a paddle board rental place. The inflatable is so much easier for a beginner. It just moves less side to side in the water and seems more stable. Not to mention being easier to transport to and from the water.

The surface of this board is very grippy on your feet. You can ride barefoot or with shoes on without worrying about slipping. The handle is perfectly placed to easily carry it once it is inflated.

Overall, a super high quality board. The material is very, very thick. I have zero concerns about it popping. I am very happy with this board and with my adventures into the sport of SUP.

text_fidelity_a:
Mars Gear Vulcan FLX Tactical Pants (Stretchable Ripstop) [[VIDEOID:b5a53a0c1b472799ef4d5a2d386537bd]] I like certain things about these and can't stand certain other ones. I cannot stand the location of the pockets. They are way too high and closer to the center. They could have cut it at more of a slant but it still is too high. You got to put your hands almost straight down into them. While this is good for stopping some pick pockets they are still open, There should be a zipper secured side pocket inside the main pocket. These don't even have side pockets at all.

Now that;s out of the way it has a lot of pockets almost too many or they are not quite big enough to hold what you need them too.. The zipper in the front doesn't stay up unless zipped all the way and locked, so you;ll end up with your fly down if your not careful and don't make sure to get the zipper all the way up, This is waste time,. in my opinion, at least. The belt loops are too small to even accommodate an 2 inch utility belt.

These are very comfortable and just about the proper warmth and cooling so they are good year round unless you live in Alaska , Siberia or any place that get below -10 degrees Fahrenheit on a regular basis. I never really got uncomfortably hot or cold in these. Some of the stitching is top notch and then there are others that are terrible. The inside of the pocket are horribly stitched and I have never seen poor stitching on any good pair of BDU's or any other military or law enforcement pant types called "tactical".

I really like the ties around the legs that allow you to tie the legs tight either around your leg inside your boots or over the outside of your boot. This is good for limiting bugs crawling up your pant legs and various other things. Now they should've used some elastic ropes with a little fast tightener in place of the cheap ribbon. There is also no loop on the waste back close to your pocket to clip anything to.

So I have decided that these are just not very good the more and more I try them out. They just feel like everything is slightly out of place. One more thing the belt loops will not accommodate any decent utility belts or even a thick well made gun belt. Not to mention I wouldn't trust the stitch-work either over any amount of time and duty. I usually wear 5.11 or Backhawk for civilian purposes and they never caused distractions. One of the two no longer is making gear and the other is slacking so I was looking for a new supplier. This was definitely not it. I think these are trying to be fashionable instead of tactical and you just cannot mix the two. Same goes for combat boots! If you are trying to look cool and have no real reason to need to wear BDU pants then go ahead and enjoy. If you require something that actually provides performance and functionality then these are not for you. I couldn't wear these to the range let alone any real situation.
text_fidelity_b: Mars Gear Vulcan FLX Tactical Pants (Stretchable Ripstop)

ODIER CO2 Inflator CO2 Pump for Bike Tires Compatible with Presta and Schrader Bicycle Valve Antifreeze Cartridge Cover Included (Rod Switch) I've got one of these similar to this one with a couple of differences.
If you know the goats head thorn, then you know the bane of my existence. I ride a scooter that has an air tire to and from work. Every week or so, I get a flat that I need to repair.

So I carry a full size spare in my backpack along with a repair kit. That includes a mini pump. That pump has a chuck that's difficult to attach because of the angle which the valve stem sticks out. And once I do get the chuck properly seated, it takes about fifty pumps to get the tire to pressure.

So I saw this co2 pump and thought I'd be a great add on to the kit. Here's how it went. The canister was simple to screw in. I could feel the seal break. The screw on chuck made it very easy to attach to the valve stem. I then barely turned the lever to the open position and that little 200x50 tire was fully inflated. Taking off the chuck, I was concerned that some air would escape since screw on chucks don't pop off immediately. No air escaped. The valve stem was a little cool to the touch.

So one difference is the angle of which the valve cap or lever comes off. This one is easier to access the valve stem. Also regarding the lever, it's a much nicer mechanism for controlling flow.

So I'd say that this was pretty successful. Simple and fast. Couldn't ask for much more.
text_fidelity_b: ODIER CO2 Inflator CO2 Pump for Bike Tires Compatible with Presta and Schrader Bicycle Valve Antifreeze Cartridge Cover Included (Rod Switch)

Stamina X Hyperextension Bench - Adjustable and Foldable Roman Chair with Smart Workout App for Home Workout - Up to 250 lbs Weight Capacity I needed something to work lower back at home, and have limited space. After reading lots of reviews, considering factors of space, budget and how users seemed to like various benches, I decided that The Stamina Hyper Bench was the way to go. It's been a week since my husband built the bench for me (thanks, honey!), which took under an hour, so let me give you my impressions.

First off, I'm 5' 3", so keep that in mind as you read. I found the bench is sturdy. It doesn't make creak, flex or make any noise when I use it, and all the feet stay firmly on the ground - no feeling whether doing back or abs that the bench might tip over. There was no damage to the paint, foam or upholstery, unlike a lot of other fitness equipment we've bought in the past. It's just a hint wobbly when not in use and rocking with your hand, but that could be our floors. Once you're on it and using it, the wobble is gone. And it had no plasticy, rubbery or chemical smell, which I appreciated. As far as value goes, it's much sturdier and easier to adjust than others I've seen at similar low price ranges.

One downside, and this only applies to people under 5' 5", is that with everything set as low as it will go, I'm a little short for the bench. It doesn't hit me at the hips but above, which isn't ideal but can be worked with. A minor downside is that doing ab crunches doesn't give much of a workout unless you're okay bending your back further back than flat, but I knew that would be the case in advance by watching the video.

BTW, this isn't showing as a verified purchase as I bought it from sports store that sent me a discount coupon.

To sum up, bench is sturdy and good quality. It arrived with no damage of any sort, has no smells, and was easy to assemble. Not ideal for those my height (5' 3"), and I wouldn't recommend it for anyone shorter, but it's a nice, useful bench and folds up nice and small to be put under a bed or in a closet. Overall for me this was a good purchase, an excellent value and good addition to my small home gym.
text_fidelity_b: Stamina X Hyperextension Bench - Adjustable and Foldable Roman Chair with Smart Workout App for Home Workout - Up to 250 lbs Weight Capacity

text_fidelity_a:
Timex Unisex The Timex Ironman run Trainer 2.0 GPS watch is a very good gps watch for runners and probably swimmers, too. I don't swim, so couldn't test that part. Despite the name "Ironman" this watch is designed for running and "approved" for swimming (that's from the Timex website where they cite "water resistant approved for 50 meters"). When I think of Ironman, I think of the big three: running, biking, and swimming. So don't let the name fool you into thinking this will connect to your bike sensors as well. That being said, if you are looking for a good watch with a heart rate monitor, this is a decent choice.

I used the watch with my existing ANT+ heart rate monitor and foot pod (both are Garmin devices). The watch synched perfectly with both. If you use a foot pod it can (and should) be calibrated so that you can then accurately track your distance and pace when you're forced to run indoors on a treadmill. The display is clean, easy to read and customizable. I also have small wrists, so was a little concerned about fit, but the watch fit comfortably on me while wearing. It is smaller and a bit more comfortable than the Garmin 310xt (the only other GPS watch I own, so compared it to that). You can even set reminders for when you need to hydrate or fuel up during a long run. Plus you can also create intervals to do interval training.

The thing I dont like about the watch is that I can't also use it for biking like I can with my [[ASIN:B0025VKUPM Garmin Forerunner 310XT]]. Which seems contrary to the fact that not only do they call it "ironman" but it even has the word "triathalon" on the watch face. however, that being said, you can use it for swimming, as I previously mentioned, as it supposedly is water resistant up to 50 meters. I am not a swimmer, so didn't try that, but I am a cyclist (as I already mentioned -- I guess I'm getting redundant here).

The GPS accuracy on the watch is pretty good. It appears to be a little more accurate than my Garmin 310xt, but the difference to me is negligible, especially if I set my Garmin to capture data every second rather than have it on "auto" - then the resulting map traces are almost identical.

Another feature that I'm not too keen on is the way you view the data. They have you use their web-based system, which I found to be too "bulky" - it has too many options and too confusing. Many of the options are only available if you pay for their premium plan. You can't even export the data into a GPX or TCX file without having paid. this is something that pretty much every other company allows for free. I did find a way around that, though. With the watch connected to your computer via the USB port, it becomes just like another USB drive on your machine and you can navigate to the folder that has your activities stored in it. Timex uses the FIT format. Luckily, Strava (a great app and website for tracking cycling and running), will import these files. Just drag the FIT file to your computer somewhere and import it into Strava. It takes a few minutes for Strava to get process the file after it imports, so if all your run information is not showing up right away, wait a few minutes and then refresh or go back to it and you should see it. Then Strava will let you export it to a GPX format which then can be imported into Runkeeper or many other popular fitness apps. Kind of some extra steps, but if you stick with this and Strava, you'll be set. Strava also has a premium (paid) feature, but I only have their basic (free) account and can do everything I need with it.

Overall, this is a really nice watch, and hopefully they will come up with a "lighter" version of their software, but for now, I am not even going to mess with it and stick with Strava.
text_fidelity_b: Timex Unisex

I recently decided it was time for an upgrade from using my parent's 1980's foam mats that have been awkwardly combined with my partner's giant trifold (and not waterproof) cushion. We camp frequently near our truck and will have a Go Fast roof top camper added in the coming months which we intend to use this in.

Here's my take - The mat is extremely durable!!! WAY more so than the air mattresses we've used before that require an electric pump. My large dogs walked across the mat several times and no marks were left. I'm not worried at all about tears or punctures with this material, and am happy to see it's rated for cold weather.
We laid three adults across it and it was comfortable but snug, so it's definitely comfortable enough for two with room to spare. The mat feels more like a memory foam topper with just the right amount of give for your hips and shoulders if you are a side sleeper. I found it comfortable to lay on my back and stomach too.

It comes with a mini foot pump attachment which easily helped us get it fully inflated (we waited about an hour or so and it self-inflated about an inch, then we got impatient and finished inflating in about 5 minutes). The valves are well-made and appear very durable. It also comes with a carry case for storage and travel.

I would definitely NOT want to lug this thing into the woods for a backpacking venture due to its size. But for car camping or tent camping close to your vehicle I absolutely recommend! The steep price tag is the only downside I can think of.

text_fidelity_a:
Retrospec Luna Exercise Ball SOO PRETTY!! This pink Pearlescent is absolutely gorgeous… And yes I’m talking about a yoga ball!!? I love the set is all inclusive… If you’ve never used a stand for yoga ball… Once you do, you won’t go back- it helps with balance and allows one to be a bit more “daring/flexible“ without angst of the ball slipping. Stand is a “click together” circular structure that once connected stays secure and actually takes effort to undo- it wont come apart otherwise.. which is exactly what you want from a stand.. stable + stationary!

The ridged ball serves a purpose which is something some don’t know about! This has “small ridges” (a few inches apart) that circumference the ball. These help keep a person in place when using (sort of like tire tread although, it’s not grabby!) I see this very beneficial for any who may need a little extra help ie. hindered with Injury, elderly or, just need or lack natural balance..

Although this has a hand pump- be prepared for it to take you a lot of effort/time to inflate- the better part of an hour.. (especially with 75cm size!!) This has a thick outer surface to keep it from puncture/bursting- which is nice to give peace of mind. This has an internal air bladder in case exterior puncture takes place.. it’s made to “break ones fall“ to the ground and let you down slower- so to speak (again, peace of mind!) But, in order to perform accurately- this must be filled taut!! and you’ll be surprised how long this can keep filling to get there. TBH, we ended up using electric pump to make quicker work of the task.. younger with more muscle may not find this as tedious. Just note: this is also compatible with an electric pump and worth getting it out for the job!!

Overall, X1 of better all inclusive sets I’ve seen- it has such an eye on quality and safety Im so impressed. Sold at $22- without hesitation I’d recommend 100%. You won’t find better..!! Hoping this info can help your decision… Stay safe!
text_fidelity_b: Retrospec Luna Exercise Ball

text_fidelity_a:
Mansader 6 Person Family Camping Tent,Waterproof Windproof with Top Rainfly,Easy Set Up,Pop Up Tent for Outdoor Camping Hiking Travel The two of us are seventy-something, live in Georgia (which is very hot and humid), and all the windows in our rental house are painted shut. In a sustained blackout, we would probably die. After the "What did our grandparents do when they didn't have air conditioning" discussion, I decided that having a few well-ventilated pop-up tent "bedrooms" outside would mimic the breezy screened sleeping porches of old, pre-air conditioning in the South.

We have separate bedrooms, so I wanted two tents for our comfort and also so there's plenty of room for the dogs who insist on sleeping with one or the other of us. Fortunately, we do have a few shady areas in our back yard where we can pitch our tent rooms. And if we have to evacuate, we can throw our tents into the back of our truck along with our camping mats, solar oven, solar generator/panels, and our kelly kettle.

Of the two tents I got, this 6-person one is larger and more durable but a little bit harder to set up; the other one is one of those that you can essentially toss in the air to unfold, then stake down. This one is going to be mine, because I'm the one the dogs want to spend the night with. Robert gets the other one because he's older with spine issues and a little less capable of putting up a tent than I am. I like that this tent fits neatly into a zippable carry bag and has everything included. We aren't likely to use it for camping, but it's a real relief to me to know we have it for our emergency "blackout kit" in case we need it.
text_fidelity_b: Mansader 6 Person Family Camping Tent,Waterproof Windproof with Top Rainfly,Easy Set Up,Pop Up Tent for Outdoor Camping Hiking Travel

Igloo Ice Cube, Ocean Blue, 14-can Capacity, 32607 ORIGINAL REVIEW: I replaced my previous Igloo cooler with this one and I really like it. The top compartment is handy. I put a camper type salt shaker in it along with a few other small items. The ice packs that I use fit perfectly and so far the handle seems like it will last. The previous igloo cooler was a bit smaller and was bought in 1992. It still works great except the handle wont stay on so it was time for a new one. I mention this because it's 24 years old and still works. that says a lot for igloo quality. I hope to get that kind of service from this cooler. The only reason the handle failed was because I stumbled and sent the cooler flying. If that had not have happened I probably would not have needed to buy this one. Igloo is rugged, last a long time and with 2 ice packs about the same size as the sides of this cooler, everything stays cool for at least 24 hours as long as it's not in direct sunlight. I'm not one for change, especially when I have a product that works and lasts. I really did need a little larger cooler so yes, I miss the old cooler but not so much because I really like this new one much better. I donated the old one and found it good home. Yes I know it's just a cooler but I used t every work day for 24 years, I got a little attached to it. They still make that model and I nearly bought it but my wife found this new one. Due to the handle issue and the fact this one is way better, I do not recommend the older version any longer in favor for this one. Yes I know run on sentences its 1 am give me a break. Buy this cooler, slap a Cowboys sticker on it and you will be happy with it.

UPDATE: Guess I was wrong about the handle lasting, it didn't. I still use it for now but plan on replacing it with a similar cooler called Igloo Quantum. This may be an updated version of the ice cube model who knows. The handle feels better but attaches the same so i expect it to fail as well. It has a few additional features like 2 places to put a lock or locks on it, useless because it can be easily cut. 2 cup holders that I find too shallow to be useful and the top compartment is half the size. The cover is thicker and opens easier from the center as opposed to the corners like the ice cube model. Lastly; it's 3 tone. Had I know the Quantum was available I would have purchased it over the ice cube model. In my opinion, they should lose the cup holders and increase the top compartment size, ensure the handle wont come off and you would have a great cooler.
text_fidelity_b: Igloo Ice Cube, Ocean Blue, 14-can Capacity, 32607

text_fidelity_a:
ARCEE Headlamp & Camping Lantern for Kids, Lightweight Portable Outdoor Indoor Tent Lamp for Children, Lanterns for Emergency, Hurricane, Power Outage, Nightlight for Kids’ Room Geared toward kids, yet anyone can benefit from it. Both the lantern and the headlamp come with preinstalled AA batteries, and CR2032 respectively. There is a spot in the description where it says "not included" but they are, and another that said they are. They are, can confirm. Just pull the little battery saver tab to activate. To access the battery compartment, you will need a tiny Phillips head screwdriver. Flat works too.

Both items are well made and durable feeling. I got that impression while unboxing. It just has a good feel, not cheap feeling. My video and pics are taken in a small dark storage room. Not actually producing colors.

The HEAD LAMP band is stretchy and adjustable. I was able to slide it onto y large 23.75" head. It is not something all that practical--no way to direct the light like one would with an adult sized head lamp but it is still useful. Good way to keep track of kid in darkness (camping, Halloween, emergency). It imparts a decent amount of direct light. I would even keep this in my car as a little emergency light. I could probably use this as a reading light if I wore it on my neck. Maybe.

TO OPERATE: press yellow button on top. THIS could be tricky for some kids and adults. As the pressure point location is directly in the convex center. Cant just press any spot on the yellow surface. Must be directly between eyes. Once that is figured out, then it is super easy.

The LANTERN is lightweight, yet robust feeling. Has TWO light options: top flashlight, forward direction. OR a diffuse lower lantern light. I think it lights up well enough for the space around. I am not sure why we would need to give a kid a spotlight (I just imagine little kiddos trying to blind others, This wont do that). This light is perfectly fine for them--in a tent, around their little area in an emergency, as their own bed side flashlight or night light of the sorts. I would use this myself in car, for sitting outside in evening, for light glow while walking around with dogs, or on my own, etc. I carry strong mag lights, but I find this little pack useful. Nice handle. Can be popped off if need be. Good base- wont easily tip over. Can take a drop to the ground, I think. Could hook this to a backpack and have lead adult or older kiddo to light up a path.

TO OPERATE: very easy, very intuitive, easy to press single button. Press to turn on upper flashlight, press again to switch it to the lantern. Another press simply turns it off.

I see they have an owl option and I love owls. My only choice was a frog. Frogs are cool, but owls are my love. I like this lantern enough to want to buy the owl for myself. I plan to keep the headlamp in my bag, and the lantern will just set out. I figured if the power goes out, it can't hurt to have extra options that don't require me to hold onto it. I can keep this on one of my end tables, and just press the button. Then I can use it to go get other supplies and such. Will make for a good glow, enough to light up area enough to be comfortable to maneuver.

----->>>>>>>In summary: This is a great little set. Fun looking, nice lights, COMES WITH BATTERIES INSTALLED, stretchy headband not limited to child use, good material, good feel, and is just refreshingly NICE product. Not cruddy feeling or looking. I do not rate on price, but I thought the full price reasonable. I bought the second one on sale (Prime Day), which was even better!

I recommend this for kids, for adults who still enjoy kid like stuff, for gift giving (I'll for practical gifts, and for a kid this would be fun and practical). They did well with including pre-installed batteries (just pull-out battery saver tag--if it doesn't fully come out, you will need to go in and take it out).
text_fidelity_b: ARCEE Headlamp & Camping Lantern for Kids, Lightweight Portable Outdoor Indoor Tent Lamp for Children, Lanterns for Emergency, Hurricane, Power Outage, Nightlight for Kids’ Room

text_fidelity_a: Graber Guardian 3 Bike Trunk Rack This is back rack number 171Z.  This bike rack is made to fit different types of vehicles such as cars, vans, and hatchbacks. It also and more importantly does not fit cars manufactured in the years 2008 and below. I HIGHLY recommend you contact Graber and ask them if this rack will fit your car before purchasing.  Even their website does not show which cars this will and will not fit.  If you go to the Graber website and click on History at the top, you will find their number.  This is not a universal rack and there are many other vehicles this rack will not accommodate so be sure to read the specifics before purchasing. It has multiple straps so that it can be adjusted to the size and recommendations of your automobile type. Considering the rack’s ability to fit (or not fit) different vehicles, the instructions are confusing. It is a lightweight rack and holds up to three bikes. It comes off a lot easier than it went on. The metal bar areas that press against the car are covered in padding so that your car does not get scratched or damaged. It is a reasonably priced rack and seems to be good quality (not great). It was not practically easy to get on, but was very easy to get off. It works great for transporting short distances, but not sure that I would trust it for an extended trip as the straps could work themselves loose.
text_fidelity_b: Graber Guardian 3 Bike Trunk Rack

text_fidelity_a:
Zefal 164 Water Bottle, 33 oz I do like having these bottles for bikepacking. It makes the difference between having to carry some kind of bladder vs making the jump between towns in the middle of summer during midday. The 1L capacity is the big appeal for me.

For me, the Camelback Podium water bottles are the best I've used. I would rate the Podium at 4 stars. I've gotten used to the annoyances and now I have really on positive associations with that water bottle .

This Zefal bottle gets additional points for capacity, and loses many points for the following criteria:
Distinct plastic taste that appears very quickly. With my other water bottles, I detect some leeching only when I leave water in the bottle overnight or longer. With the Zefal, it's almost immediate. That worries me.

Requires too much force to seal the lid. On my first bikepacking trip with these, I kept wasting water because my first squeeze after each stop would go on my face and jersey, in addition to my mouth. I'm used to it now and I know how hard I need to muscle on the lids.

No jet nozzle. This is the same basic design as water bottles had 40 years ago. It's not horrible - it works like it's supposed to; OTOH if the Camelback is 4 stars then this design is worth much less.

Branding: I simply feel strange about branding on really low-end items. IDK - maybe I'm afraid that people with think that I think this is great water bottle? Maybe I shouldn't take that out on the product. I definitely don't mind the Camelback logo, no matter how outlandish and counter to my design taste, and yet with these bottles even the conservative branding seems to be in bad taste.

Overall, this bottle simply fails to meet my criterion for good cycling gear: its interface/use is not transparent. I.e. instead of simply using it routinely / out of habit / on muscle memory, I'm always aware of opening the valve, tasting plastic, and remembering to close the valve as I return it to the cage. Gear that I consider over the threshold for good sinks down out of sight much faster than my habit formation with these - assuming I will ever get used to them. At this point it seems more likely that next summer I'll set out of find a better solution to this same problem.

I simply don't like these bottles.

Overall this feels like many levels of quality down from the Camelback bottles. I find the capacity appealing and really nothing else. It's like the quip about cookie-cutter, drywall box "McMansion": it's not home, but it's much.
text_fidelity_b: Zefal 164 Water Bottle, 33 oz

text_fidelity_a:
Sunlite Cloud-9 Bicycle Suspension Cruiser Saddle, Cruiser Gel, Tri-color Black If you have the type of seat post where the saddle rails are sandwiched/clamped between two contoured plates this saddle might not work on your seat post clamp. This saddle comes with one of those rotary, rotating, claw-type clamps and the saddle likely works fine with that included clamp. However better bike seat posts can't use the included claw clamp type -- they must use their own sandwich-type. Technically, this saddle still should still mount but the distance between the rails was too wide. If you are confused about the difference do a web search for 'bike seat rail clamp' and you'll see the two different families of clamps.

I would have thought that the measured distance between saddle rails would be standardized but the rails on this saddle were just a very few millimeters too wide for both my sandwich-type clamps (it failed to mount on the two different seat post clamps I tried it on). The distance could maybe be lessened by clamping the rails, in a vice, for example, or using some other tool but I decided to return it rather than mess with it..

Otherwise it seemed okay, maybe quite a bit on the stiff side for a gel saddle.
text_fidelity_b: Sunlite Cloud-9 Bicycle Suspension Cruiser Saddle, Cruiser Gel, Tri-color Black
